title: Observability: token-level tracing, metric refinements, dashboard and alert tuning
author: Evelyn Park
description: Motivation: We continue to see noisy alerts and poor visibility into per-token cost/latency regressions for the serving runtime. This PR adds token-level tracing hooks, refines token-level metrics ingested into our metrics pipeline, updates Grafana dashboards to show cost/latency breakdowns by token position and model variant, and tunes alert thresholds to reduce noise while preserving regression detection. Summary of changes: added tracing spans at token emission points, exported token latency and token compute-cost estimators to prometheus, added aggregation rules for token-level p99/p95/p50 by model+route, added a new cost-per-token dashboard with heatmaps and timeseries, adjusted alert thresholds for token-latency and token-cost surge alerts, added explanatory notes and dashboards links in the incident playbook, and added unit/integration tests for the new metrics endpoints. Checklist: - [x] Add token-level spans and ensure low overhead instrumentation - [x] Export token-level metrics (latency, compute_millis, estimated_cost) - [x] Add Prometheus recording rules and alerts - [x] Update Grafana dashboards and dashboards provisioning - [x] Add docs/playbook notes for alert interpretation and runbooks - [x] Tests: unit + integration + canary validation in perf-canary lab Rollback plan: Revert dashboard provisioning and recording rules first (no infra changes), revert instrumentation if we observe CPU overhead > 5% in canary. Performance: microbenchmarks show ~0.6% p99 latency overhead at median request sizes and <1.5% CPU overhead in perf canary with tracing off-by-default in production. Tracing is enabled for sampling rate 1% by default and configurable per-tenant. Related: ENG-4241 (token-level observability epic), ENG-4310 (alert noise reduction).

review_comments: Aisha Khan (2026-02-11): Nice work overall. Two questions: 1) Can we make the tracing sampling rate adjustable per-tenant via config? 2) Are the recording rules performant on prometheus?

Evelyn Park (2026-02-12): Reply: Sampling is configurable via tenant config (default 1%). Recording rules were validated in the perf-canary cluster; we added shard_by: ['model','route'] to reduce cardinality and included aggregation windows to avoid high scrape cardinality.

release_notes: - Added token-level tracing spans with low-overhead sampling (configurable per-tenant). - Exported token-level latency and estimated cost metrics to Prometheus. - New Grafana dashboards: token-cost heatmap and token-latency breakdowns by model and route. - Tuned token-latency and token-cost alerts to reduce noise while preserving regression detection. - Added playbook notes and runbook links for interpreting token-level alerts.
